summary: The keeper state machine (watch → patch vs rebuild → save with atomic swap), plus notebook upkeep: refreshKbNotesIndex derives the kb-notes.json sidecar single-flight (queued via refreshingKb/kbRefreshQueued) at watch start, on .raw batches, and post-save. Graph-invisible coupling added in #85: refreshKbNotesIndex calls regenerateKbViewIfPresent, which re-renders an EXISTING notebook index.html (via kbView from src/kb/view.ts, open:false) on every notes refresh so a browser reload shows latest notes without re-running `kb view`. It never CREATES index.html (that stays the explicit `kb view`) and is best-effort/try-caught so a render failure cannot wedge the keeper.

summary: IndexManager owns the live in-memory code index + orchestrates patches/rebuilds/notebook-sidecar refresh. refreshKbNotesIndex (fires on every notebook .raw change, debounced+single-flighted) now also calls mechanicalSymbolRepair right after saving the sidecar, passing it in memory (no redundant disk read) — so a new single-file note's anchor symbols get backfilled within the same debounce cycle instead of waiting for `kb repair`/`init`. Self-triggering (its own kbWrite re-fires this refresh) is capped at MAX_AUTO_REPAIR_STREAK=3 consecutive fixing passes; a pass that fixes nothing resets the streak to 0, so the idle case is free.

summary: Keeper state machine: watch, patch-vs-rebuild, atomic cache save, plus the notebook sidecar refresh. Verified 2026-08-03 on autoMechanicalSymbolRepair, which fires right after every kb-notes-index rebuild and passes the just-built sidecar in memory. Its MAX_AUTO_REPAIR_STREAK=3 guard is one-way: once the streak reaches the cap the method returns before running, so the pass that would reset the streak never happens and auto-backfill stays off for the whole keeper lifetime. That is the safe direction but was silent; it now logs once naming `coldstart kb repair`. Confirmed with a live keeper that a healthy repo fires exactly once and the next refresh resets the streak to 0.

summary: Keeper state machine: watch, patch-vs-rebuild, atomic cache save, plus the notebook sidecar refresh and (2026-08-23) the co-change sidecar refresh. autoMechanicalSymbolRepair fires right after every kb-notes-index rebuild and passes the just-built sidecar in memory; its MAX_AUTO_REPAIR_STREAK=3 guard is one-way — once the streak reaches the cap the method returns before running, so the pass that would reset it never happens and auto-backfill stays off for the keeper's lifetime (safe direction, now logged once naming `coldstart kb repair`). refreshCoChange is deliberately keyed on git HEAD rather than on the debounced file batch: history only changes when a commit lands, so re-walking on every patch would burn ~600ms for a byte-identical result. It is called from startWatching (seed) and from inside scheduleCacheSave's getGitHead().then, which is the one place the keeper already knows HEAD moved.
